questions.title: Coverings of the testis
questions.question: The testis is covered with all the following EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The tunica vaginalis is a genuine covering of the testis: a serous sac derived from the processus vaginalis of the peritoneum that clothes the anterior and lateral surfaces of the organ.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The tunica albuginea is the tough dense fibrous capsule immediately deep to the tunica vaginalis and is a true covering of the testis.
explanations.C: Correct. The testis has three coats from outside in — the tunica vaginalis (serous), the tunica albuginea (dense fibrous capsule) and the tunica vasculosa (inner loose vascular layer). There is no "tunica propria" among the testicular coverings; that term refers to the peritubular boundary tissue of the seminiferous tubule, not a coat of the whole organ, so it is the required exception.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The tunica vasculosa is the innermost vascular layer lining the deep aspect of the tunica albuginea and the septa, and is a true covering of the testis.

questions.learning_objective: List the three coverings of the testis (tunica vaginalis, albuginea, vasculosa) and recognise that "tunica propria" is not among them.

field_notes.keySource: printed p.7 Dr Kandeel answer table (Q1 = C)
field_notes.kasr: Dr Kandeel male histology bank, p.2

questions.title: The tunica albuginea of the testis
questions.question: The middle covering layer of the testis, formed of dense fibrous connective tissue, is called:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The tunica vaginalis is the outer serous coat, not the dense fibrous middle layer.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The tunica vasculosa is the inner loose vascular layer, not a dense fibrous coat.
explanations.C: Incorrect. "Tunica propria" is the peritubular tissue of the seminiferous tubule, not a coat of the testis.
explanations.D: Correct. The tunica albuginea is the thick capsule of dense fibrous (collagenous) connective tissue lying deep to the tunica vaginalis. It thickens posteriorly to form the mediastinum testis and sends fibrous septa that divide the gland into lobules, making it the tough middle covering that gives the testis its firm consistency.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the tunica albuginea as the dense fibrous capsule of the testis that forms the mediastinum and septa.

questions.title: Cells of the seminiferous tubule
questions.question: The seminiferous tubule contains all the following cells EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Sertoli (sustentacular) cells are the tall supporting cells that line the seminiferous tubule and form its blood-testis barrier, so they are a true tubular cell.
explanations.B: Correct. The seminiferous tubule is lined by the germinal (spermatogenic) epithelium — spermatogonia, spermatocytes and spermatids — together with Sertoli cells. Leydig (interstitial) cells lie OUTSIDE the tubule, in the loose interstitial connective tissue between tubules, where they secrete testosterone. They are therefore not a cell of the seminiferous tubule and are the required exception.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Spermatids are haploid germ cells in the adluminal compartment of the tubule and are a true tubular cell.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Spermatogonia are the diploid stem cells resting on the basal lamina inside the tubule and are a true tubular cell.

questions.learning_objective: State that Leydig cells are interstitial and are not part of the seminiferous tubule epithelium.

field_notes.keySource: printed p.7 Dr Kandeel answer table (Q4 = B)
field_notes.kasr: Dr Kandeel male histology bank, p.2

questions.title: The spermatogenic cell line
questions.question: All the following cells are spermatogenic cells EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Spermatogonia are the diploid stem cells at the start of the spermatogenic series, so they are spermatogenic cells.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Spermatocytes (primary and secondary) are the meiotic members of the spermatogenic line.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Spermatids are the haploid post-meiotic germ cells that mature into spermatozoa, so they are spermatogenic cells.
explanations.D: Correct. The spermatogenic (germ) line comprises spermatogonia, spermatocytes and spermatids. Sertoli cells are the somatic SUPPORTING (sustentacular) cells of the tubule; they nourish and protect the germ cells and form the blood-testis barrier but never become sperm, so they are not spermatogenic cells and are the required exception.

questions.learning_objective: Distinguish the spermatogenic germ-cell line from the supporting Sertoli cell.

field_notes.kasr: Dr Kandeel male histology bank, p.2

questions.title: Origin of primary spermatocytes
questions.question: Which of the following cells divide and differentiate into primary spermatocytes?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Pale type A spermatogonia are the renewing stem cells; they divide to maintain the stem pool and to give type B cells, but they do not become primary spermatocytes directly.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Dark type A spermatogonia are the reserve (dormant) stem cells and do not differentiate directly into spermatocytes.
explanations.C: Correct. Type B spermatogonia are the last mitotic generation of the spermatogonial series; each divides and then differentiates into a primary spermatocyte, which enters the long prophase of the first meiotic division. Type A (pale/dark) cells are the stem compartment that ultimately gives rise to type B, but it is the type B cell that becomes the primary spermatocyte.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Spermatids are the haploid product of the second meiotic division, downstream of the spermatocytes, not their precursor.

questions.learning_objective: State that type B spermatogonia differentiate into primary spermatocytes.

field_notes.keySource: printed p.7 Dr Kandeel answer table (Q7 = C)
field_notes.kasr: Dr Kandeel male histology bank, p.2

questions.title: Chromosomes after the first meiotic division
questions.question: At the end of the first meiotic division, each daughter cell contains:

explanations.A: Correct. Meiosis I is the reductional division: homologous chromosomes separate, so each secondary spermatocyte receives 23 chromosomes. Each of those chromosomes still consists of two sister chromatids joined at the centromere — a "dyad" or d-chromosome. So the product is 23 double-structured (dyad) chromosomes, halving the chromosome number while the DNA content is still 2C.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The chromosome number is halved to 23 at meiosis I, not kept at 46.
explanations.C: Incorrect. 46 is the diploid number of the primary spermatocyte before meiosis I, not the number in each daughter cell after it.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Single-chromatid (monad, s-) chromosomes appear only after meiosis II, when the sister chromatids separate; after meiosis I the 23 chromosomes are still dyads.

questions.learning_objective: State that the first meiotic division yields cells with 23 dyad (double-chromatid) chromosomes.

field_notes.kasr: Dr Kandeel male histology bank, p.2

questions.title: Source of androgen-binding protein
questions.question: Androgen binding protein (ABP) is secreted by:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Leydig cells secrete testosterone, not androgen-binding protein; they supply the androgen that ABP then binds.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Type B spermatogonia are germ cells that differentiate into primary spermatocytes; they have no secretory role for ABP.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Type A spermatogonia are the stem/reserve germ cells and do not secrete ABP.
explanations.D: Correct. Androgen-binding protein is a secretory product of the Sertoli cell, made under FSH stimulation. By binding testosterone (supplied by the neighbouring Leydig cells), ABP keeps a high local androgen concentration inside the seminiferous tubule and carries testosterone into the lumen and along the ducts, which is essential for spermatogenesis.

questions.learning_objective: Identify androgen-binding protein as a Sertoli-cell secretion that concentrates testosterone in the seminiferous tubule.

field_notes.kasr: Dr Kandeel male histology bank, p.2

questions.title: Ploidy of the primary spermatocyte
questions.question: In the seminiferous tubules, the primary spermatocytes:

options.A: Contain a diploid number of chromosomes
options.C: Are the smallest of the spermatogenic cells
options.D: Divide by mitosis to give secondary spermatocytes

explanations.A: Correct. The primary spermatocyte arises from a type B spermatogonium and has NOT yet completed a reduction division, so it still carries the diploid (2n = 46) chromosome number. It then enters the long prophase of meiosis I; only when meiosis I is complete does the chromosome number fall to the haploid 23 of the secondary spermatocyte.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Spermatogonia rest on the basal lamina; once a cell becomes a primary spermatocyte it has moved into the adluminal compartment above the Sertoli tight junctions.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The primary spermatocyte is in fact the LARGEST cell of the spermatogenic series, not the smallest.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Primary spermatocytes give secondary spermatocytes by the FIRST MEIOTIC (reductional) division, not by mitosis.

questions.learning_objective: State that the primary spermatocyte is diploid before it completes the first meiotic division.

questions.title: Cytology of the Leydig cell
questions.question: Interstitial cells of Leydig contain all the following EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Correct. Leydig cells are steroid-secreting cells, so their cytoplasm is ACIDOPHILIC (eosinophilic), not basophilic. Basophilia reflects abundant rough endoplasmic reticulum / ribosomes (protein-secreting cells); a steroid-secreting cell instead has eosinophilic cytoplasm rich in smooth ER and lipid, so "basophilic cytoplasm" is the false statement and the required exception.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Like other steroid-secreting cells, Leydig cells contain mitochondria with tubular (tubulovesicular) cristae, which house steroidogenic enzymes.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Leydig cells have abundant smooth endoplasmic reticulum, the site of cholesterol-to-testosterone conversion, so this is a true feature.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Numerous lipid droplets store the cholesterol substrate for steroidogenesis and are a characteristic Leydig-cell feature.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise the acidophilic, steroid-secreting cytology of the Leydig cell (smooth ER, tubular-cristae mitochondria, lipid droplets).

field_notes.keySource: printed p.7 Dr Kandeel answer table (Q14 = A)
field_notes.kasr: Dr Kandeel male histology bank, p.2

questions.title: Type A spermatogonia
questions.question: There is only one true answer about type A spermatogonia:

options.A: They give rise directly to primary spermatocytes
options.C: They are of dark and pale types

explanations.A: Incorrect. Type A cells give rise to type B spermatogonia; it is the type B cell that becomes the primary spermatocyte, not type A directly.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Type A spermatogonia are the earliest stem cells of the line; they do not develop from the much later secondary spermatocytes.
explanations.C: Correct. Type A spermatogonia exist as two forms: dark type A (Ad), the dormant reserve stem cells, and pale type A (Ap), the renewing stem cells that divide to maintain the pool and to produce type B spermatogonia. This dark/pale distinction is the defining feature of type A cells.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Spermatogonia divide by MITOSIS; meiosis begins only at the primary spermatocyte stage, so type A cells do not undergo meiotic division.

questions.learning_objective: State that type A spermatogonia occur as dark (reserve) and pale (renewing) types.

field_notes.kasr: Dr Kandeel male histology bank, p.3

questions.title: Location of Leydig cells
questions.question: Leydig cells are present in:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The seminal vesicle is an accessory gland of the duct system and contains no Leydig cells.
explanations.B: Correct. Leydig (interstitial) cells lie in the loose vascular connective tissue in the angular spaces BETWEEN the seminiferous tubules of the testis. There, close to blood capillaries, they secrete testosterone under luteinising-hormone (ICSH) control. Their interstitial position is what distinguishes them from the intratubular Sertoli and germ cells.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The bulbourethral (Cowper's) gland is a mucus-secreting accessory gland and contains no Leydig cells.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The prostate is an accessory gland with fibromuscular stroma; Leydig cells are confined to the testicular interstitium.

questions.learning_objective: Locate Leydig cells in the interstitial tissue between the seminiferous tubules.

questions.title: Phases of spermiogenesis
questions.question: Spermiogenesis is divided into the following phases EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The Golgi phase is the first phase of spermiogenesis, in which pro-acrosomal granules from the Golgi coalesce into the acrosomal vesicle.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The acrosomal (cap) phase, in which the acrosome spreads to cap the anterior nucleus, is a true phase of spermiogenesis.
explanations.C: Correct. Spermiogenesis is classically divided into four phases: Golgi, cap (acrosomal), acrosomal/tail and maturation phase. There is no separately named "mitochondrial phase"; the mitochondria simply aggregate around the proximal flagellum to form the middle-piece sheath during the tail/maturation stages, so "mitochondrial phase" is the required exception.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The maturation phase, in which excess cytoplasm is shed as the residual body, is a true final phase of spermiogenesis.

questions.learning_objective: Name the phases of spermiogenesis (Golgi, cap/acrosomal, maturation) and recognise there is no separate "mitochondrial phase".

field_notes.keySource: printed p.7 Dr Kandeel answer table (Q30 = C)
field_notes.kasr: Dr Kandeel male histology bank, p.4

questions.title: Control of spermatogenesis
questions.question: All the following are necessary for the control of spermatogenesis EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect. FSH acts on Sertoli cells to support spermatogenesis and to drive androgen-binding-protein and inhibin production, so it is required.
explanations.B: Correct. TSH (thyroid-stimulating hormone) controls the thyroid gland and has no direct role in the local control of spermatogenesis. The regulators of spermatogenesis are FSH and LH-driven testosterone (androgen), the Sertoli products androgen-binding protein and inhibin (feedback on FSH), so TSH is the required exception.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Inhibin, secreted by Sertoli cells, feeds back on the pituitary to modulate FSH output and is part of the control loop.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Androgen-binding protein maintains the high intratubular testosterone that spermatogenesis needs, so it is part of the control system.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Androgen (testosterone from Leydig cells) is essential for spermatogenesis and for maintaining the germinal epithelium.

questions.learning_objective: List the regulators of spermatogenesis (FSH, androgen, ABP, inhibin) and exclude TSH.

field_notes.kasr: Dr Kandeel male histology bank, p.4

questions.title: Features of Sertoli cells
questions.question: Sertoli cells are characterised by all the following EXCEPT:

options.B: They divide during the reproductive period
options.D: They contain abundant smooth endoplasmic reticulum

explanations.A: Incorrect. Adjacent Sertoli cells are joined by occluding (tight) junctions near their base; these junctions create the blood-testis barrier, so this is a true feature.
explanations.B: Correct. Sertoli cells are a STABLE, non-dividing population: they stop proliferating at puberty and their number is then fixed for life, which sets the upper limit on sperm output. Saying they "divide during the reproductive period" is therefore false and is the required exception.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Sertoli cells secrete androgen-binding protein (as well as inhibin and anti-Mullerian hormone), so this is a true feature.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Sertoli cells have abundant smooth endoplasmic reticulum (and rER), consistent with their varied synthetic and steroid-handling roles.

questions.learning_objective: State that Sertoli cells do not divide after puberty (their number is fixed).

field_notes.keySource: printed p.7 Dr Kandeel answer table (Q46 = B)
field_notes.kasr: Dr Kandeel male histology bank, p.4

questions.title: Secretions of Sertoli cells
questions.question: Sertoli cells secrete all the following EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Inhibin is a Sertoli-cell peptide that feeds back on the pituitary to reduce FSH secretion, so it is a true Sertoli product.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Anti-Mullerian hormone (Mullerian-inhibiting substance) is secreted by Sertoli cells; in the fetus it causes regression of the Mullerian ducts.
explanations.C: Correct. Testosterone is synthesised by the interstitial LEYDIG cells, not by Sertoli cells. Sertoli cells secrete inhibin, anti-Mullerian hormone and androgen-binding protein and support spermatogenesis, but they do not make testosterone, so testosterone is the required exception.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Androgen-binding protein is a Sertoli-cell secretion that concentrates testosterone within the tubule, so it is a true Sertoli product.

questions.learning_objective: List the Sertoli-cell secretions (inhibin, anti-Mullerian hormone, ABP) and exclude testosterone (a Leydig product).

field_notes.kasr: Dr Kandeel male histology bank, p.5

questions.title: Epithelium of the vas deferens
questions.question: The vas deferens is lined with:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The mucosa of the vas deferens is pseudostratified, not a single layer of simple columnar cells.
explanations.B: Correct. The vas (ductus) deferens is lined by a pseudostratified columnar epithelium whose principal cells carry stereocilia, continuing the epithelial pattern of the epididymis. This epithelium sits on a folded mucosa surrounded by the characteristic thick three-layered muscular coat that propels sperm during emission.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Simple cuboidal epithelium lines small ducts such as the rete testis, not the vas deferens.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Transitional epithelium (urothelium) lines the urinary tract, not the vas deferens.

questions.learning_objective: State that the vas deferens is lined by pseudostratified columnar epithelium with stereocilia.

field_notes.keySource: printed p.7 Dr Kandeel answer table (Q38 = B)
field_notes.kasr: Dr Kandeel male histology bank, p.4

questions.title: Characteristics of the prostate gland
questions.question: The prostate gland is characterised by all the following EXCEPT:

options.C: It is penetrated by the urethra
options.D: Its capsule is rich in smooth muscle fibres

explanations.A: Incorrect. The prostate is built of 30-50 branched tubulo-alveolar glands arranged in mucosal, submucosal and main groups, so this is true.
explanations.B: Correct. Prostatic secretion is a thin, milky, slightly acidic fluid rich in acid phosphatase, citric acid, fibrinolysin and prostate-specific antigen — it is NOT a mucous secretion. Mucus is the product of the bulbourethral (Cowper's) glands, so "secretes a mucous fluid" is the false statement and the required exception.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The prostatic urethra runs through the gland, so the prostate is genuinely penetrated by the urethra.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The prostatic capsule and stroma are fibromuscular, rich in smooth muscle whose contraction expels the secretion at ejaculation, so this is true.

questions.learning_objective: State that prostatic secretion is a thin milky fluid, not mucous (mucus is a Cowper's-gland product).

field_notes.keySource: printed p.7 Dr Kandeel answer table (Q41 = B)
field_notes.kasr: Dr Kandeel male histology bank, p.4

questions.title: Characteristics of the seminal vesicle
questions.question: The seminal vesicle is characterised by all the following EXCEPT:

options.A: It is a pair of coiled tubular glands
options.B: Its mucosa is lined with simple cuboidal epithelium
options.C: Its smooth muscle is arranged as inner circular and outer longitudinal
options.D: It secretes a yellowish, alkaline, viscid fluid

explanations.A: Incorrect. Each seminal vesicle is a single, highly coiled tubular gland, so the pair are coiled tubular glands — a true feature.
explanations.B: Correct. The seminal vesicle is lined by a pseudostratified/simple COLUMNAR secretory epithelium thrown into an elaborate honeycomb of folds, not by simple cuboidal cells. Calling the lining "simple cuboidal" is therefore the false statement and the required exception.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The wall has a smooth muscle coat of inner circular and outer longitudinal layers that contracts at emission, so this is true.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Seminal-vesicle fluid is a yellowish, alkaline, fructose-rich viscid secretion that forms much of the ejaculate volume, so this is true.

questions.learning_objective: State that the seminal vesicle is lined by a folded columnar (not simple cuboidal) secretory epithelium.

field_notes.kasr: Dr Kandeel male histology bank, p.4

questions.title: Epithelium of the prostatic urethra
questions.question: The prostatic urethra is lined with:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Stratified squamous epithelium lines the terminal (navicular) part of the penile urethra, not the prostatic urethra.
explanations.B: Correct. The prostatic urethra — the first part of the male urethra, passing through the prostate — is lined by transitional epithelium (urothelium), continuous with that of the urinary bladder above it. Only more distally does the urethral lining change to pseudostratified/stratified columnar and finally stratified squamous.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Stratified columnar epithelium lines much of the membranous and penile urethra, not the prostatic part.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Pseudostratified columnar epithelium appears more distally in the urethra; the prostatic urethra is urothelium.

questions.learning_objective: State that the prostatic urethra is lined by transitional epithelium (urothelium).

field_notes.kasr: Dr Kandeel male histology bank, p.5

questions.title: The rete testis
questions.question: The network of anastomosing tubules present within the mediastinum testis and lined with cuboidal epithelium is called:

explanations.A: Correct. The rete testis is the labyrinth of anastomosing channels housed within the fibrous mediastinum testis, lined by a simple cuboidal epithelium (often with a single apical cilium). It receives sperm from the straight tubules (tubuli recti) and drains into the efferent ductules.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The tubuli recti (straight tubules) are short straight ducts that carry sperm from the seminiferous tubules INTO the rete; they are not the anastomosing network itself.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The ductuli efferentes leave the rete to reach the epididymis and lie outside the mediastinum; they are not the mediastinal network.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Only the rete testis fits the description of an anastomosing network within the mediastinum, so "all of the above" is wrong.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the rete testis as the anastomosing channel network in the mediastinum testis lined by simple cuboidal epithelium.

field_notes.kasr: Dr Kandeel male histology bank, p.5

questions.title: The corpus spongiosum
questions.question: This structure is ventrally located in the body of the penis, terminates by the glans penis and is penetrated by the penile urethra:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The two corpora cavernosa lie dorsally in the body of the penis and do not transmit the urethra.
explanations.B: Correct. The corpus spongiosum is the single midline erectile column on the VENTRAL aspect of the penile body; the penile (spongy) urethra runs through it, and distally it expands to form the glans penis. Its venous erectile spaces are smaller and more uniform than those of the corpora cavernosa, which keeps the urethra patent during erection.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The corpus luteum is an ovarian endocrine structure, unrelated to the penis.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Corpora amylacea are concretions inside prostatic alveoli, not an erectile body of the penis.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the corpus spongiosum as the ventral penile erectile body that transmits the urethra and forms the glans.

field_notes.keySource: printed p.7 Dr Kandeel answer table (Q57 = B)
field_notes.kasr: Dr Kandeel male histology bank, p.5

questions.title: The bulbourethral (Cowper's) glands
questions.question: These are two tubulo-alveolar glands present outside the membranous urethra of the male and empty into the first part of the penile urethra:

explanations.A: Correct. The bulbourethral (Cowper's) glands are paired, pea-sized compound tubulo-alveolar mucous glands lying in the deep perineal pouch outside the membranous urethra. Their ducts pierce the perineal membrane and open into the first (bulbous) part of the penile urethra, where their clear mucoid secretion lubricates it before ejaculation.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The single prostate surrounds the prostatic urethra; it is not a pair of glands outside the membranous urethra.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Bowman's glands are serous olfactory glands in the nasal mucosa, unrelated to the male genital tract.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The seminal vesicles lie behind the bladder and empty (via the ejaculatory ducts) into the prostatic urethra, not into the penile urethra.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the bulbourethral (Cowper's) glands as paired tubulo-alveolar glands opening into the penile urethra.

questions.title: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
questions.question: The prostatic acini which undergo hyperplasia in old age are:

options.D: Both the mucosal and the submucosal acini

explanations.A: Incorrect. The main (peripheral) group is the site of prostatic CARCINOMA, not of the benign age-related hyperplasia.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The submucosal group is involved, but not alone; the mucosal group enlarges as well.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The mucosal group is involved, but not alone; the submucosal group enlarges with it.
explanations.D: Correct. Benign prostatic hyperplasia of old age arises in the inner, periurethral MUCOSAL and SUBMUCOSAL glands. Their enlargement compresses the prostatic urethra and causes obstructive urinary symptoms. This inner-gland origin contrasts with prostatic carcinoma, which typically arises in the outer main (peripheral) glands.

questions.learning_objective: State that benign prostatic hyperplasia affects the mucosal and submucosal (inner, periurethral) prostatic glands.

field_notes.kasr: Dr Kandeel male histology bank, p.5
